problem:
Consider the following matrices:

$$
K=[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ -2 & 6\end{aligned}],\,J=[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{2} \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Given that $K=PJ{P}^{-1},$ find ${3}^{K/2}.$

feedback.problem:
Consider the following matrices:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-5 & 4 \\ -9 & 7\end{aligned}],\,J=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Given that $M=PJ{P}^{-1},$ find $\operatorname{ln}⁡M.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Given a function $f$ and matrices $A$ and $S,$ where $S$ is invertible, we have

$$
f(SA{S}^{-1})=S\cdot f(A)\cdot {S}^{-1}.
$$

For $f(x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡x$ and the given matrix $M,$ we have

$$
\operatorname{ln}⁡M=\operatorname{ln}⁡(PJ{P}^{-1})=P\cdot (\operatorname{ln}⁡J)\cdot {P}^{-1}.
$$

Now, since $J$ is a Jordan block with $1$s on the main diagonal, we have

$$
\operatorname{ln}⁡J=[\begin{aligned}f(1) & {f}^{′}(1) \\ 0 & f(1)\end{aligned}].
$$

The derivative of $f$ is ${f}^{′}(x)=\frac{1}{x}.$ So, we get

$$
\operatorname{ln}⁡J=[\begin{aligned}f(1) & {f}^{′}(1) \\ 0 & f(1)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1) & \frac{1}{(1)} \\ 0 & \operatorname{ln}⁡(1)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Also, the inverse of $P$ is

$$
{P}^{-1}=\frac{1}{2\cdot 2-3\cdot 1}[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡M & =P\cdot (\operatorname{ln}⁡J)\cdot {P}^{-1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 & 2 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & 4 \\ -9 & 6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
